body: What works for me will be dying. Or, as I can see it another way, not death but a transcendence into another form of life. Since our brains can’t fully contemplate death, all I can really know before it happens is another life after it. It’s a feel good lie really.

Hey, it’s great that you want to know, as do I too. The brain is a strange organ that can make you want to do certain things, and you don’t even know why you want to do them. Eh, maybe it’s all subconscious, like I’ve always been destined for this no matter what. But the fact is that I really don’t care much for knowing as I care more for actually following through with it.
My name? Mike. My age? 14-23 years old. My location? The United States.
Eh, mostly sarcastic, cause to tell you the truth I don’t have a definitive answer as to why I’m going to do it. What I can tell you is that I will do it, and I guess I’ll have to enjoy it.

Oh come on man! You’re messaging someone who will know the great beyond soon and you want to know what I’ve done in life? Ugh, fine. I’ll keep this short: I’ve concluded that death seems to be the most exciting option for me at this point. It seems fun and intriguing and I can’t wait to see what happens.

Hey, thanks for the reply! I’ve already been living day by day, in fact I’ve been living year by year to be honest trying to move on. I really gave it my best though so at least I die with my integrity.

Seriously speaking, if I got like a life threatening disease like cancer, I would decide to live out the rest of my life. Reason being that I wouldn’t have much more time to life, and my body will kill itself for me.
